# Delete A Single Note

This endpoint deletes a note. It's permanent.

The note ID goes in the path.

# List events

List the events in an account. Authenticate with an API key in the `Authorization` header.

`GET /v3/events`

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `limit` | Events per page, up to 200. |

A successful response returns an `events` array and a `next_cursor` string. The `next_cursor` field is empty on the last page.

An invalid key returns `401`.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ORBITLY_KEY" https://api.example.com/v3/events
```

notes: No authentication, no response fields, and 'hook' replaces 'webhook'.

# Create a webhook

Create a webhook to receive events at your own URL.

`POST /v3/webhooks`

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | Yes | The HTTPS endpoint that receives events. |
| `events` | array | No | Event types to send. Defaults to all. |

```json
{"url": "https://hooks.example.com/orbitly"}
```

The call returns the new hook. A bad URL returns `422`.

# Get a note

Get one note by its ID. Authenticate with an API key in the `Authorization` header.

`GET /v2/notes/{id}`

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Yes | The note ID. |

Please note that the response contains the note's `title`, `body`, and `updated_at` fields, and if the note sits in an archived workspace the response also contains an `archived` flag set to true.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $FERNBOOK_KEY" https://api.example.com/v2/notes/n_123
```

If the note does not exist, the API returns `404`. The code mentioned above also covers deleted notes, i.e. notes in the trash.

# Delete a webhook

Delete a webhook to stop event deliveries to its URL. Authenticate with an API key in the `Authorization` header.

`DELETE /v3/webhooks/{id}`

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Yes | The webhook ID. |

A successful call returns `204` with an empty body. An unknown ID returns `404`.

```bash
curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $ORBITLY_KEY" https://api.example.com/v3/webhooks/wh_123
```

# List notes

List the notes in a workspace, newest first. Authenticate with an API key that has the `notes:read` scope.

`GET /v2/notes`

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | Yes | The workspace to list. |
| `limit` | integer | No | Notes per page, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20. |

A successful response returns a `notes` array and a `next_cursor` string. Each note has an `id`, a `title`, and an `updated_at` timestamp.

An invalid key returns `401`. An unknown workspace returns `404`.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $FERNBOOK_KEY" "https://api.example.com/v2/notes?workspace_id=ws_1"
```

# Rotate an API key

Rotate a key to replace it without downtime. Authenticate with an admin API key.

`POST /v2/keys/{id}/rotate`

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Yes | The key to rotate. |
| `grace_period` | integer | No | Seconds the old key keeps working. Defaults to 3600. |

The response returns the new key in a `key` field. The developer should probably store the new key before the grace period ends.

A key that is already rotating returns `409`.

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FERNBOOK_ADMIN_KEY" https://api.example.com/v2/keys/k_1/rotate
```

notes: 'Authorization header' needs backticks, and 'fifteen' must be a numeral.

# Upload an attachment

Upload a file and attach it to a note. Authenticate with an API key in the Authorization header.

`POST /v2/notes/{id}/attachments`

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Yes | The note ID. |
| `file` | file | Yes | The file to upload, up to 25 MB. |

The response returns the attachment `id`, `size`, and `content_type`. Files over the limit return `413`. You can attach up to fifteen files to one note.

```bash
curl -F "file=@diagram.png" -H "Authorization: Bearer $FERNBOOK_KEY" https://api.example.com/v2/notes/n_1/attachments
```
